# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 91 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 91 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_091_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9 — Mountains Nine through Twelve

**1** "The ninth mountain — utterly barren, infested with snakes — represents those who believed but got stained with every kind of sin; they never consistently followed through on repentance, and they never really bonded with other believers. **2** Many of them are hollow inside — all that sin has emptied them out. Some never repented at all. **3** The snakes you saw? Those are their own sins eating away at them from within, consuming and destroying them. These people's sins are destroying not just themselves but their whole households." **4** "The tenth mountain with those great spreading trees giving full shade, and cattle resting and chewing in their shadow — these represent those who believed and are truly blessed. They never wander from God; they rest in him continuously with joy, always pondering the Lord and his truth, deeply rooted in God." **5** "The eleventh mountain with trees loaded with all kinds of fruit — these represent those who suffered for the name of the Lord, who went through every hardship with gladness and a willing heart, giving their very lives." **6** "The twelfth mountain — gleaming white — represents young children and those with pure minds who never once entertained a wicked thought, who had no knowledge of what evil even was, who simply lived in innocence their whole lives." **7** "That is why the mountains are so different and varied — because these peoples are different from each other. Each group has been given a specific window for repentance; anyone who repents within that window will live with God, provided they repent before the tower is complete. **8** If the tower is finished and they still haven't repented, there is no place for them in it. Only those fitted in before completion have a place."

---

*PNEUMA renders the final four mountains with increasing beauty — from serpent-infested desert to pure-white innocence. The eschatological urgency of vv. 7-8 is emphasized.*
